Description

Join our team as a SeniorCommercial Lines Specialist, helping small businesses find the right coverage through consultative sales and tailored insurance solutions. In this fast-paced role, youll prospect new opportunities, build lasting client and referral relationships, and work with multiple carriers to deliver quality coverage and service.

Hiring locations: We are seeking candidates based in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C.

Responsible for prospecting, generating, developing, and managing a book of small commercial insurance business. Counsels and advises prospects and policyholders on matters of protection and coverage. Is responsible for a specific volume of quality new business quoted and written within company guidelines. This role combines prospecting and new-business production with consultative sales, quoting through multiple carriers, and coordinating policy placement and renewals.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Source and develop new small commercial accounts (typically business accounts with revenues under $10M) through prospecting, referrals, networking, and inbound leads.
  • Utilizes coverage knowledge to counsel and advise prospects and existing policyholders on matters of protection and coverage based on a needs and exposure assessment by obtaining data and relative information concerning their business. Recommend appropriate insurance solutions (BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds).
  • Conducts front-line underwriting risk evaluation in accordance with established rules and guidelines. Prepare and present quotes and proposals by obtaining/comparing quotes from multiple carriers using agency management systems, CRM and carrier panel rating platforms.
  • Meets goals for volume of quality new business and cross sell opportunities quoted and written within company guidelines.
  • Works collaboratively with internal and agency partners to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.
  • Build relationships and trust with referring agents within the region to build COI/lead generation streams
  • Provide timely service for endorsements, cancellations, audits, and claims liaison as needed.
  • Stay current on carrier appetite, new products, underwriting guidelines, and industry trends.
Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with common small commercial products: BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds
  • Experience with networking, prospecting for new business and driving top of funnel leads from various sources
  • Experience using agency management systems, comparative raters
  • Strong verbal and written communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills
  • Property & Casualty license (or progress toward them. You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience selling small commercial lines in an independent agency or carrier distribution channel
  • Proven track record of meeting production targets; demonstrated book of business or established referral sources

Skills & Competencies:

  • Consultative sales approach and client-focused problem solving.
  • Demonstrated analytical skills to understand complex coverage details and underwriting guidelines clearly to small-business owners
  • Collaborative mindset and comfortable working in a high-volume agency environment.
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication, persuasion and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to build a sphere of influence in the community and participate in community networking activities
  • Effective time management and ability to work well independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate numerous computerized data entry systems or other relevant applications simultaneously while advising customers
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent business background plus a minimum of 1-3 years of insurance or sales/service-related work experience.

In this fast-paced role, youll prospect new opportunities, build lasting client and referral relationships, and work with multiple carriers to deliver quality coverage and service.

Hiring locations: We are seeking candidates based in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C.

Responsible for prospecting, generating, developing, and managing a book of small commercial insurance business. Counsels and advises prospects and policyholders on matters of protection and coverage. Is responsible for a specific volume of quality new business quoted and written within company guidelines. This role combines prospecting and new-business production with consultative sales, quoting through multiple carriers, and coordinating policy placement and renewals.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Source and develop new small commercial accounts (typically business accounts with revenues under $10M) through prospecting, referrals, networking, and inbound leads.
  • Utilizes coverage knowledge to counsel and advise prospects and existing policyholders on matters of protection and coverage based on a needs and exposure assessment by obtaining data and relative information concerning their business. Recommend appropriate insurance solutions (BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds).
  • Conducts front-line underwriting risk evaluation in accordance with established rules and guidelines. Prepare and present quotes and proposals by obtaining/comparing quotes from multiple carriers using agency management systems, CRM and carrier panel rating platforms.
  • Meets goals for volume of quality new business and cross sell opportunities quoted and written within company guidelines.
  • Works collaboratively with internal and agency partners to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.
  • Build relationships and trust with referring agents within the region to build COI/lead generation streams
  • Provide timely service for endorsements, cancellations, audits, and claims liaison as needed.
  • Stay current on carrier appetite, new products, underwriting guidelines, and industry trends.
Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with common small commercial products: BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds
  • Experience with networking, prospecting for new business and driving top of funnel leads from various sources
  • Experience using agency management systems, comparative raters
  • Strong verbal and written communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills
  • Property & Casualty license (or progress toward them. You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience selling small commercial lines in an independent agency or carrier distribution channel
  • Proven track record of meeting production targets; demonstrated book of business or established referral sources

Skills & Competencies:

  • Consultative sales approach and client-focused problem solving.
  • Demonstrated analytical skills to understand complex coverage details and underwriting guidelines clearly to small-business owners
  • Collaborative mindset and comfortable working in a high-volume agency environment.
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication, persuasion and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to build a sphere of influence in the community and participate in community networking activities
  • Effective time management and ability to work well independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate numerous computerized data entry systems or other relevant applications simultaneously while advising customers
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent business background plus a minimum of 1-3 years of insurance or sales/service-related work experience.
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

In 2022, Comparion Insurance Agency was created to transition former Liberty Mutual exclusive agents to an agency that delivers a unique value proposition to carriers with over 2,000 agents in approximately 180 cities in 44 states. We offer customers 50 insurance companies with product breadth including auto, home, life, pet, renters, umbrella, jewelry and much more. We use our scale to deliver a first-rate customer experience through consultative insurance experts located in their communities.

Our Leadership team has over 200 years of cumulative insurance experience. At Comparion, we have a philosophy of staying close to our customers and agents, so sales leadership is located throughout the country in our larger storefronts. Comparion is owned and backed by Liberty Mutual Group, a Fortune 100 company, founded in 1912

Liberty Mutual is an equal opportunity employer. We will not tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, veteran's status, pregnancy, genetic information or on any basis prohibited by federal, state or local law.

Description

Join our team as a SeniorCommercial Lines Specialist, helping small businesses find the right coverage through consultative sales and tailored insurance solutions. In this fast-paced role, youll prospect new opportunities, build lasting client and referral relationships, and work with multiple carriers to deliver quality coverage and service.

Hiring locations: We are seeking candidates based in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C.

Responsible for prospecting, generating, developing, and managing a book of small commercial insurance business. Counsels and advises prospects and policyholders on matters of protection and coverage. Is responsible for a specific volume of quality new business quoted and written within company guidelines. This role combines prospecting and new-business production with consultative sales, quoting through multiple carriers, and coordinating policy placement and renewals.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Source and develop new small commercial accounts (typically business accounts with revenues under $10M) through prospecting, referrals, networking, and inbound leads.
  • Utilizes coverage knowledge to counsel and advise prospects and existing policyholders on matters of protection and coverage based on a needs and exposure assessment by obtaining data and relative information concerning their business. Recommend appropriate insurance solutions (BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds).
  • Conducts front-line underwriting risk evaluation in accordance with established rules and guidelines. Prepare and present quotes and proposals by obtaining/comparing quotes from multiple carriers using agency management systems, CRM and carrier panel rating platforms.
  • Meets goals for volume of quality new business and cross sell opportunities quoted and written within company guidelines.
  • Works collaboratively with internal and agency partners to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.
  • Build relationships and trust with referring agents within the region to build COI/lead generation streams
  • Provide timely service for endorsements, cancellations, audits, and claims liaison as needed.
  • Stay current on carrier appetite, new products, underwriting guidelines, and industry trends.
Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with common small commercial products: BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds
  • Experience with networking, prospecting for new business and driving top of funnel leads from various sources
  • Experience using agency management systems, comparative raters
  • Strong verbal and written communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills
  • Property & Casualty license (or progress toward them. You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience selling small commercial lines in an independent agency or carrier distribution channel
  • Proven track record of meeting production targets; demonstrated book of business or established referral sources

Skills & Competencies:

  • Consultative sales approach and client-focused problem solving.
  • Demonstrated analytical skills to understand complex coverage details and underwriting guidelines clearly to small-business owners
  • Collaborative mindset and comfortable working in a high-volume agency environment.
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication, persuasion and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to build a sphere of influence in the community and participate in community networking activities
  • Effective time management and ability to work well independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate numerous computerized data entry systems or other relevant applications simultaneously while advising customers
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent business background plus a minimum of 1-3 years of insurance or sales/service-related work experience.

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$96,700.00 - $159,600.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

The Sales Executive Team is dedicated to navigating and managing a high performing sales culture in person and/or virtually which contributes to the overall success of the Select business. The team executes on industry-leading sales strategies aligned with business objectives, builds effective relationships with customers, distribution partners and fellow employees, and creates tactical sales plans for profitable growth through extensive product knowledge and state of the art sales and influencing tactics. The team also uses digitally advanced strategies to move the business forward, leads the relationships with our aggregator/networking groups, and partners with the agent to imbed into higher producing revenue streams. As a Sales Executive, Select, you will manage and develop a moderately complex group of Travelers agency assignments/territories, optimize growth within defined new business, retention and profitability goals and deliver success within Travelers' framework of Corporate values. You will act as a brand ambassador to sell the Travelers value proposition to distribution partners. This position is an outside sales position where assigned distribution relationships within the geographic territory tend to be best served through an in-person sales strategy.

What Will You Do?

  • Develop and implement comprehensive sales strategies to expand and manage a portfolio of business, with the objective of driving profitable growth.
  • Own assigned territory, including business development, leveraging performance metrics to create annual plans and manage territorial performance.
  • Conduct in-depth agency diagnostics to assess performance and identify growth opportunities.
  • Facilitate agency appointments and build long-term relationships through office visits (both in person and virtual).
  • Prospect, onboard and set performance goals for new agencies, while providing training and support.
  • May pre-qualify accounts as needed.
  • Influence agency partners through effective communication and negotiation skills.
  • Collaborate with internal teams, such as, Product and Underwriting to ensure alignment of sales strategies with business objectives.
  • Understand Travelers Enterprise focus and seize opportunities to cross-sell Travelers products by discussing with business partners in other lines. May identify book transfer opportunities.
  • Develop knowledge of competitor products and capabilities and local market trends.
  • Utilize advanced data and analytics for sales decisions and performance measurement, leveraging extensive knowledge of Travelers' systems and platforms to support the sales process.
  • Leverage AI technologies to optimize industry processes, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation, while continuously learning and adapting to emerging AI trends and tools.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in sales, marketing, business or related field.
  • Four or more years of insurance sales or related experience managing a book of business, driving significant sales growth, achieving sales targets, conducting agency diagnostics and utilizing digital sales tools.
  • Certified Insurance Counselor (CIC) (or willingness to pursue).
  • Strong knowledge of Travelers products and general Property & Casualty marketplace.
  • Strong influencing and negotiation skills to encourage agency partners to adopt Travelers products and services.
  • Proven ability to collaboratively build and maintain relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders both internally and externally.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to define goals and priorities and meet these goals in a timely manner.
  • Exceptional organizational skills to manage complex tasks and priorities to meet sales goals and deadlines effectively.

What is a Must Have?

  • Three years of professional experience in sales, sales support or relevant insurance field.
  • Must live in the territory that they manage and have the ability to travel up to 75% of the time.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. What Is the Opportunity?

The Risk Control organization consists of motivated professionals with diverse risk engineering expertise across multiple commercial insurance disciplines. By delivering high quality risk assessments and consultative services, we help clients better understand and mitigate their risks while empowering underwriters with the insights needed to make informed account selection and pricing decisions that drive profitable growth. As a Risk Control Sr Consultant, CAG, you will apply your well-developed technical competencies in risk assessment and loss control by independently consulting with clients on moderate to high complexity risks across multiple industries and lines of coverage.

What Will You Do?

  • Maintain a consistent field presence, spending approximately 20% to 50% of the time with customers. Overnight and extended trips may be required depending on business need. Car and air travel may be necessary.
  • Independently prepare, conduct, and complete technically detailed risk assessments of moderate to high complexity to evaluate potential hazards and risk. Complexity is defined by industry, account size, number of locations, and exposure type.
  • Apply advanced consultative skills with clients to implement recommended risk control measures to reduce, mitigate, or prevent losses.
  • Build and maintain collaborative relationships with clients and internal stakeholders to ensure coordinated, high-quality, consultative service focused on risk reduction across all accounts.
  • Share technical knowledge and provide guidance to peers to support team effectiveness and continuous learning.
  • Stay current on emerging industry trends, regulatory developments, and best practices by actively pursuing relevant training, certifications, and continuing education opportunities.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in environmental health and safety, construction management, basic sciences, or a related technical field.
  • Six or more years of multiline risk control or risk management experience in the property and casualty insurance industry.
  • Certification in one or more relevant industry-recognized designations or licenses such as ASP, ARM, CSP, CFPS, CIH, CPE, etc.
  • Verbal and written communication skills.
  • Critical thinking and analytical skills.
  • Influencing and relationship-building skills.
  • Organizational and time management skills.

What is a Must Have?

  • Five years of experience in safety, risk control/management, or a related field, such as occupational/environmental health and safety, science, engineering, construction, manufacturing, or relevant military experience.
  • Valid driver's license.
  • Where applicable, must have or obtain appropriate certification to meet state-specific requirements within agreed upon timeframe.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $215,000 to $480,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Radnor, PA
  • Experience: 5+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Work from Home; Boston, MA (Massachusetts); Buffalo, NY (New York); Concord, NH (New Hampshire); Dover, NH (New Hampshire); Edison, NJ (New Jersey); Hartford, CT (Connecticut); New York, NY (New York); Paramus, NJ (New Jersey); Parsippany, NJ (New Jersey); Philadelphia, PA (Pennsylvania); Pittsburgh, PA (Pennsylvania); Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Rochester, NY (New York); US Northeast; Windsor, CT (Connecticut)

Work Arrangement:

Remote : Work at home employee residing outside of a commutable distance to an office location.

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76606

The Role at a Glance

As Retirement Sales Director, you will be responsible for driving growth through new retirement plan sponsor acquisition, with a primary focus on mid to large market plans ($50M+ in assets). In this role, you will develop and execute a territory business plan designed to achieve ambitious sales, AUM, and market share goals across your assigned geography. You will serve as a key external representative, building and expanding relationships with retirement plan consultants, advisors, brokers, and plan sponsors. This is a highly consultative, relationship driven sales role that requires deep retirement industry knowledge, disciplined pipeline management, and close collaboration with internal partners to deliver comprehensive retirement solutions and exceptional client outcomes.

What you'll be doing

Drive Growth & New Business Acquisition
• Lead new retirement plan sponsor acquisition with a focus on plans with $50M+ in assets
• Develop and execute a territory and prospecting strategy to meet or exceed annual sales and AUM targets
• Identify, qualify, and cultivate prospective plan sponsors through proactive outreach, referrals, networking, and consultant relationships
• Manage the full sales cycle, from initial engagement through finalist presentations, pricing, contract negotiation, and close.
Build and Deepen Influencer Relationships
• Build, maintain, and grow strong relationships with retirement plan consultants, advisors, brokers, and other centers of influence impacting mid to large market plan decisions
• Increase territory penetration by strengthening partnerships with influential specialists and consulting firms
• Position the organization as a preferred retirement provider through consistent engagement, education, and thought leadership
Deliver Consultative Retirement Solutions
• Conduct needs based discovery with plan sponsors to understand fiduciary objectives, plan design, investments, participant outcomes, and service expectations
• Present tailored retirement solutions, including recordkeeping, investments, managed accounts, and financial wellness offerings
• Clearly articulate value propositions around fiduciary governance, plan outcomes, fee reasonableness, and participant engagement
Territory & Sales Execution Excellence
• Manage a large geographic territory, executing external wholesale sales programs that drive revenue and market share growth
• Conduct in person and virtual meetings such as due diligence sessions, consultant updates, one on one meetings, and industry sponsorships
• Represent the organization at industry conferences, client events, and networking functions
• Maintain accurate pipeline, activity tracking, and forecasting in CRM and sales reporting systems
• Forecast sales activity and revenue with discipline, transparency, and accountability
• Effectively manage expense budgets to maximize territory coverage and sales impact
Collaboration & Operational Discipline
• Partner closely with internal stakeholders including operations, product, client service, core market counterparts, and consultant relations teams to support opportunities and ensure seamless onboarding and issuance
• Ensure sold business is properly processed from point of sale through implementation
• Uphold the highest standards of professionalism, ethics, and compliance, adhering to all policies, procedures, and cultural expectations

What we're looking for

Must-Haves:
• Minimum of 5+ years of experience in Defined Contribution retirement plan sales and/or relationship management, with direct alignment to the responsibilities of this role
• Bachelor's degree required, or equivalent professional experience (4 additional years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree)
• Ability to obtain FINRA Series 6, Series 63, and Life & Health licenses within 120 days of hire
• Confident and effective communicator with strong written and verbal communication skills
• Demonstrated ability to communicate credibly and knowledgeably with senior leaders, both internally and externally
• Strong presentation capabilities with a proven track record of influencing stakeholders at all levels through clear, logical, and well informed discussions
• Advanced relationship management skills, including the ability to partner collaboratively with internal teams and build trusted relationships with external clients
• Willingness and ability to travel up to 50%

Nice-to-Have:
• Strong working knowledge of ERISA rules and regulatory requirements governing retirement plans

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through November 20th, 2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume

What's it like to work here?

At Lincoln Financial, we love what we do. We make meaningful contributions each and every day to empower our customers to take charge of their lives. Working alongside dedicated and talented colleagues, we build fulfilling careers and stronger communities through a company that values our unique perspectives, insights and contributions and invests in programs that empower each of us to take charge of our own future.

What's in it for you:

  • Clearly defined career tracks and job levels, along with associated behaviors for each of Lincoln's core values and leadership attributes

  • Leadership development and virtual training opportunities

  • PTO/parental leave

  • Competitive 401K and employee benefits

  • Free financial counseling, health coaching and employee assistance program

  • Work arrangements that work for you

The pay range for this position is $215,000 - $480,000 with anticipated pay for new hires between the minimum and midpoint of the range and could vary above and below the listed range as permitted by applicable law. The base pay is just one component of Lincoln's total rewards package for employees. In addition, the role may be eligible for the Annual Incentive Program, which is discretionary and based on the performance of the company, business unit and individual. Other rewards may include long-term incentives, sales incentives and Lincoln's standard benefits package.

About The Company

Lincoln Financial (NYSE: LNC) helps people to confidently plan for their version of a successful future. We focus on identifying a clear path to financial security, with products including annuities, life insurance, group protection, and retirement plan services.

With our 120-year track record of expertise and integrity, millions of customers trust our solutions and service to help put their goals in reach.

Lincoln Financial Distributors, a broker-dealer, is the wholesale distribution organization of Lincoln Financial. Lincoln Financial is the marketing name for Lincoln Financial Corporation and its affiliates including The Lincoln National Life Insurance Company, Fort Wayne, IN, and Lincoln Life & Annuity Company of New York, Syracuse, NY. Lincoln Financial affiliates, their distributors, and their respective employees, representatives and/or insurance agents do not provide tax, accounting or legal advice.

Lincoln is committed to creating an inclusive environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

Follow us on Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube. For the latest company news, visit our newsroom.

Be Aware of Fraudulent Recruiting Activities

If you are interested in a career at Lincoln, we encourage you to review our current openings and apply on our website. Lincoln values the privacy and security of every applicant and urges all applicants to diligently protect their sensitive personal information from scams targeting job seekers. These scams can take many forms including fake employment applications, bogus interviews and falsified offer letters.

Lincoln will not ask applicants to provide their social security numbers, date of birth, bank account information or other sensitive information in job applications. Additionally, our recruiters do not communicate with applicants through free e-mail accounts (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail) or conduct interviews utilizing video chat rooms. We will never ask applicants to provide payment during the hiring process or extend an offer without conducting a phone, live video or in-person interview. Please contact Lincoln's fraud team at fraudhotline@lfg.com if you encounter a recruiter or see a job opportunity that seems suspicious.

Additional Information

This position may be subject to Lincoln's Political Contribution Policy. An offer of employment may be contingent upon disclosing to Lincoln the details of certain political contributions. Lincoln may decline to extend an offer or terminate employment for this role if it determines political contributions made could have an adverse impact on Lincoln's current or future business interests, misrepresentations were made, or for failure to fully disclose applicable political contributions and or fundraising activities.

Any unsolicited resumes or candidate profiles submitted through our web site or to personal e-mail accounts of employees of Lincoln Financial are considered property of Lincoln Financial and are not subject to payment of agency fees.

Lincoln Financial ("Lincoln" or "the Company") is an Equal Opportunity employer and, as such, is committed in policy and practice to recruit, hire, compensate, train and promote, in all job classifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin or disability. Opportunities throughout Lincoln are available to employees and applicants are evaluated on the basis of job qualifications. If you are a person with a disability that impedes your ability to express your interest for a position through our online application process, or require TTY/TDD assistance, contact us by calling (866) 922-6543.

Job.JobDescription:
Job Description

Account Executive II, Power & Renewables – Aon Global Natural Resources

Are you energized by the transition to a low‑carbon future? Do you want to sit at the center of the global Power & Renewables market, advising some of the world's most sophisticated utilities and renewables companies on their most complex risks? If so, this could be the role for you!

Join Aon's industry‑leading Global Natural Resources team as a Senior Account Executive III focused on Power & Renewables, and help our clients make better decisions in an era of unprecedented change.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better—to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. We are united through trust as one inclusive team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

In this role, you will be the strategic quarterback for a portfolio of major Power & Renewables clients. You will:

  • Own and grow key client relationships, engaging directly with senior decision-makers while remaining a trusted, day‑to‑day partner for client teams.
  • Lead the end‑to‑end renewal process, assembling and guiding cross‑functional Aon teams to craft and implement tailored renewal strategies.
  • Partner closely with Brokers to design and deliver innovative risk transfer and placement strategies that reflect current and emerging market dynamics.
  • Orchestrate critical relationships between clients, Aon account and risk services teams, and insurers to drive differentiated outcomes.
  • Ensure the client service team deeply understands each client's business, risk profile, and goals—and that our service model and economic framework are aligned to them.
  • Lead stewardship planning and delivery, clearly demonstrating the value Aon brings through insights, outcomes, and execution.
  • Manage overall account profitability, taking a value‑based approach to scope, pricing, and the Client Service Standards
  • Structure and negotiate Aon's compensation for services, whether fee‑ or commission‑based, ensuring transparency and alignment.
  • Educate clients on risk management and risk transfer options, market conditions, and key trends in the Power & Renewables landscape, supported by benchmarking and analyzer data.
  • Mobilize the right Aon experts and resources when clients face unusual or high‑severity situations, such as major claims or new project developments.
  • Collaborate across geographies (including international markets), functions, and business divisions to build coordinated solutions and capture growth opportunities.
  • Coordinate invoicing and receivables for assigned clients, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and a high‑quality client experience.

How this opportunity is different

This is a high‑impact, visible role at the intersection of global power, infrastructure, and risk. You will:

  • Serve as the primary relationship owner for some of Aon's most important Power & Renewables clients.
  • Lead and mentor cross‑disciplinary client service teams to deliver outstanding service and unlock new value for clients.
  • Play a strategic role in helping clients navigate the energy transition, new technologies, evolving regulatory pressures, and increasingly sophisticated risk landscapes.
  • Build and grow a profitable book of business, with room to innovate on service, structure, and solutions in partnership with Aon's broader Global Natural Resources platform.

Through strategic advice, differentiated service, and compelling insight, you will showcase the full power of Aon to our clients—and help define what “best in class” looks like in the Power & Renewables sector.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • 10–15+ years of Property & Casualty (P&C) experience, with a strong track record serving complex, multinational clients.
  • Deep experience managing large, sophisticated accounts in the Power, Renewables, and/or broader Natural Resources sector.
  • Proven ability to lead client relationship strategy, drive growth, and manage profitability across a portfolio of accounts.
  • Strong organizational, interpersonal, and project management skills, with the ability to prioritize effectively and manage multiple complex initiatives simultaneously.
  • Sharp critical thinking and executive‑level communication skills; able to translate complex concepts into clear, compelling narratives for a range of stakeholders.
  • High level of digital fluency, including advanced use of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) and comfort with data‑driven insights.
  • Active Property & Casualty license required.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred, or equivalent years of relevant industry experience.

Pay Transparency Laws

The salary range for this position is $150,000 to $185,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on your education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. Salary may also be adjusted based on geographic location.

This role is eligible to participate in one of Aon's annual incentive plans, including a discretionary bonus and production incentives in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus and production incentives varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

If you're ready to help shape the future of Power & Renewables risk management—and to grow your career with a global leader—we encourage you to apply!

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.

Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon's discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance, various types of leaves of absence, paid time off, including 12 paid holidays throughout the calendar year, 15 days of paid vacation per year, paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies.

Who We Are:

NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. Summary of the Role

We are seeking an Investment Analyst to join our Wealth Management team. This is an excellent opportunity for an analytical, intellectually curious professional who is passionate about investments and interested in building a long-term career focused on leading client portfolios.

The Investment Analyst will interact directly with advisors and investment professionals to support portfolio analysis, investment research, client meeting preparation, and ongoing portfolio management activities. The role will initially focus on developing a strong understanding of our investment approach and supporting senior team members, with the opportunity to grow into a more client-facing position and participate directly in investment conversations with clients.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Investment Analysis & Portfolio Support

  • Conduct investigation and evaluation across a broad range of asset classes, investment strategies, funds, and managers.
  • Assist with portfolio construction, asset allocation, rebalancing, and implementation activities.
  • Supervise client portfolios, investment performance, allocations, and risk exposures.
  • Analyze public and private investment opportunities and help translate research into actionable recommendations.
  • Support investment due diligence and ongoing manager research.
  • Research capital markets, economic developments, and investment trends that may impact client portfolios.
  • Prepare investment analysis and recommendations for consultants and experienced investment professionals.

Advisor & Client Support

  • Partner closely with advisors to prepare for client meetings from an investment perspective.
  • Attend client meetings alongside advisors and senior portfolio management professionals.
  • Gain investment-related action items from meetings and ensure timely follow-through.
  • Prepare portfolio reports, investment materials, market commentary, and other information used in client discussions.
  • Assist with client investment inquiries by researching questions and developing thoughtful responses.
  • Build the knowledge and presentation skills necessary to gradually engage in direct financial discussions with clients.
  • Develop an understanding of each client's objectives, risk tolerance, liquidity needs, tax considerations, and overall financial goals.

Research & Investment Recommendations

  • Evaluate investment managers, funds, strategies, and other investment opportunities.
  • Prepare portfolio recommendations, investment proposals, and due diligence materials.
  • Synthesize complex investment information into clear insights for advisors, clients, and internal collaborators.
  • Give research and analysis to broader investment discussions.
  • Stay informed on financial markets, economic conditions, investment products, and industry developments.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong analytical and quantitative capabilities.
  • Genuine interest in investments, capital markets, portfolio management, and wealth management.
  • Understanding of fundamental investment concepts, including asset allocation, diversification, risk, and portfolio construction.
  • Ability to interpret financial and investment data and communicate findings clearly.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to lead multiple priorities and work optimally in a collaborative environment.
  • Strong interpersonal skills with a curiosity about developing client-facing capabilities.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn from seasoned investment experts.
  • High level of integrity, judgment, and discretion when working with sensitive client information.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, or a similar area of study, with equivalent experience also accepted.
  • 3-5 years of experience in wealth management, investment management, investment research, financial analysis, or a related field preferred.
  • Experience conducting investment or securities research is a plus.
  • Exposure to equities, fixed income, mutual funds, ETFs, alternative investments, or portfolio analytics is helpful.
  • Interest in advancing professional credentials, including the Series 65, with a willingness to pursue additional certifications such as the Series 7 and 66, CFP, or CFA.

Job Description

Early Careers Launch - Broking

Commercial Risk - NPG Trucking

Launch Your Career in Broking

Aon is looking for soon-to-be graduates and recent graduates to join our Early Careers Launch Development Program as Brokers, with opportunities across Commercial Risk and Reinsurance. You do not need to be an insurance expert on day one. Through our Launch Program and on-the-job learning, you will learn how brokers help clients understand risk, navigate insurance and reinsurance markets, and make better decisions, that support resilience and growth.

Location: Little Rock, Arkansas

As a Broker, you will build the skills, confidence and market knowledge needed to translate complex risk exposures into structured insurance programs and serve as a credible intermediary between clients and insurers.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What is Commercial Risk

Commercial Risk Aon's Commercial Risk team helps organizations around the world identify, understand, and manage the risks that could impact their people, assets, and performance. We partner with clients across industries to design and deliver innovative risk and insurance solutions - from property and casualty to cyber and specialty risks - using data, analytics, and deep market insight to help them make better decisions and protect their business.

What You Will Do

As a Broker, you will build hands-on broking experience while developing an understanding of how risk, markets, clients and strategy come together to create value for clients. Technology, including AI, Aon's risk analyzers and global delivery teams increasingly support routine execution, allowing Brokers to focus earlier on commercial judgment, market strategy and client value.

Analyze Risk and Build Market Insight

  • Assess risk exposures using data, analytics and market intelligence while learning to validate results across coverage lines.
  • Conduct market analysis to benchmark pricing, identify coverage gaps and support effective program recommendations.

Support Market Strategy and Placements

  • Help prepare market submissions, renewal materials, placement documentation and client deliverables.
  • Engage insurers and underwriters to secure competitive pricing and terms, applying market knowledge where AI-suggested terms need tailoring.
  • Build experience coordinating renewals, reviewing contracts and maintaining accurate documentation for smaller placements and account activity.

Build Client Relationships and Advisory Skills

  • Participate in client meetings, presentations and follow-up materials with growing confidence.
  • Leverage technology, data analytics, and market insights to translate complex risk information into clear, actionable recommendations that help clients make informed business decisions.
  • Build trust as a credible point of contact while developing client and market relationships.

Coordinate Projects and Improve How Work Gets Done

  • Support placement workflows across broking, account management, analytics, operations, specialist teams and global delivery partners.
  • Review documents and client materials for accuracy, consistency and quality before they are used with markets or clients.
  • Identify opportunities to improve broking processes and support efficient client delivery.

Qualifications 

  • College Seniors graduating between Spring 2026 to Spring 2027 with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0
  • Please Note: For this role you must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

The Launch Development Program

Launch is a structured 10-month Early Career development program that combines meaningful work, business learning, professional development and relationship-building across Aon. The program helps you build a strong foundation for a long-term broking and advisory career through:

  • On-the-job learning with brokers, client teams, account managers and solution line specialists.
  • Business and professional development in Commercial Risk, Reinsurance, client service, communication, collaboration, problem solving and commercial awareness.
  • Exposure to data, analytics and technology that support risk assessment, market analysis, workflow coordination and client-ready recommendations.
  • Networking, mentorship and coaching opportunities to build relationships across Aon and develop your career path.

What Will Help You Succeed and Grow

We are looking for candidates who are curious, motivated and excited to learn. Through the Launch Program, you will continue developing the same skills and capabilities that support a successful broking and advisory career, including:

  • An interest in business, risk, insurance, reinsurance, analytics, finance, economics, client service or global markets.
  • A desire to pursue a career in Commercial Risk and/or Reinsurance - Broking.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally with a range of stakeholders.
  • Analytical and critical thinking, problem-solving ability and attention to detail.
  • A collaborative mindset, alongside initiative, adaptability and a willingness to contribute as part of a team.
  • Excellent organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Confidence using technology and a willingness to learn new tools, internal AI platforms and technology-enabled ways of working.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
  • Interpersonal skills and the ability to build positive working relationships with colleagues, clients and external partners.
  • Initiative and a commitment to continuous learning, growth and professional development.

Position Overview

NFP is seeking an experienced Account Executive, Broker (P&C) for its South Central region. This position is responsible for broking new and renewal business for a varied portfolio of energy and non-energy clients, including middle-market and large, complex accounts. The broker will handle all aspects of the placement from strategy development through policy delivery, ensuring client needs are promptly and accurately addressed, deadlines are met, and service standards are achieved.

This is a full-time, hybrid position based in Austin or Houston, Texas. Regular in-office presence is required to support collaboration and strong partnerships across teams.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

  • Lead marketing for a book of energy and non-energy P&C clients in the South Central region, partnering with account teams and clients to align on strategy, timelines, and execution.
  • Execute national and regional broking strategies to support optimal client outcomes, retention, and profitable growth.
  • Develop strategies for at-risk accounts and identify book-of-business optimization opportunities.

Operational Process

  • Drive placement strategy and execution, including client needs assessment, program design, carrier negotiation, and marketing execution.
  • Coordinate complete and timely submissions, respond to carrier questions, analyze quotes, and present clear recommendations to clients.
  • Determine appropriate coverage based on the client's risk profile, business objectives, and risk appetite.
  • Develop creative solutions for complex placement scenarios and manage the placement cycle in accordance with NFP's service standards and timelines.
  • Use NFP's strategic carriers, panels, and preferred wholesalers to secure appropriate coverage, terms, and pricing.
  • Prepare proposals, coverage and policy comparisons, and related client materials; review binders and policies for accuracy.
  • Use data and analytics to provide meaningful program insight and support informed placement decisions.
  • Support prospect activity, retention, and appropriate cross-sell and up-sell opportunities.

Talent Development

This is an exciting opportunity to work alongside some of the most experienced and respected Insurance Professionals in the industry. Our team specializes in managing complex indemnity structures, handling high-volume transaction activity, and delivering sophisticated risk analysis for clients operating at the highest levels of the construction sector.

This hybrid role (2–3 days onsite weekly) from a local Aon office. We are considering applicants in Chicago, Detroit, St Louis, Indianapolis and Minneapolis.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like:

  • Collaborate with senior team members to develop coverage strategies and marketing initiatives for both renewals and prospective business opportunities.
  • Respond promptly and accurately to client requests, inquiries, and service needs.
  • Prepare and maintain up-to-date documentation for new business and renewals.
  • Analyze client-specific risk exposures and coverage needs; develop and present tailored marketing proposals.
  • Build and maintain strong, positive relationships with the underwriting community, particularly with key partner markets.
  • Process and/or issue, as applicable, new policies, renewals, endorsements, additions, deletions, and cancellations.
  • Review and proofread all documentation, ensure accurate signatures are obtained, and distribute materials as needed.
  • Calculate premium adjustments and other related figures for insurance and provider documentation.
  • Lead, monitor, and report on ongoing insurance or risk retention programs, ensuring they meet performance goals.
  • Manage daily tasks and key assignments using appropriate technology tools and platforms.

How this opportunity is different

This isn't a typical Account Executive role. At the core of our team is a deep bench of industry-leading expertise and a collaborative culture that empowers you to grow quickly and meaningfully. You'll be working with high-performing professionals on some of the most complex and high-stakes surety programs in the market—programs that demand creativity, agility, and strategic thinking. You'll have the chance to lead, influence, and drive measurable impact while developing a long-term career path in a firm that values technical excellence, innovation, and leadership development.

Skills and experience that will lead to success:

  • 7+ years of relevant experience in Property & Casualty insurance, with a strong preference for expertise in Construction Surety Bonds.
  • Proven ability to build strong rapport and collaborate effectively with high-level clients and stakeholders.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to meet deadlines, manage multiple tasks, and adapt quickly to shifting priorities.
  • Exceptional attention to detail, with a commitment to reviewing work thoroughly and participating in peer reviews.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and proactively, while also contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks based on urgency and volume, while maintaining flexibility in a fast-paced setting.
  • Solid mathematical and analytical reasoning skills to support risk analysis and premium calculations.
  • Deep relationships with national and regional carriers active in the Surety and P&C markets.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate complex information to clients and team members.
  • Strong digital literacy, including proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook) and experience creating compelling client presentations.
  • Commitment to maintaining compliance with all Aon policies and applicable regulatory requirements.

Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of industry experience.

  • Must have the willingness to obtain an active Property and Casualty license within four months of hire (90 days)

Captive Client Leader | Aon Captive & Insurance Management (ACIM)

Are you a client leader who turns strong relationships into long‑term strategic value?

Do you thrive in complex client environments where success depends on judgment, influence, and cross‑functional collaboration?

Join us to help clients make better captive and risk financing decisions!

This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work from our Burlington, Vermont office and from home in line with Aon's U.S. smart working policy.

This role must be based in Vermont. Candidates will need to already reside in the state or be willing to relocate.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

This role exists to strengthen client outcomes through consultative captive leadership. As a Captive Client Services Director, you will act as the principal interface between captive clients and Aon, ensuring clients receive high‑quality service, strategic insight, and access to the right expertise across the business. You will help clients make better decisions about captive performance, risk financing strategy, and long‑term value creation.

Typical activities include:

  • Leading strategic client engagement for a portfolio of captive clients, acting as the primary relationship lead for senior executives
  • Running annual account planning discussions aligned to client priorities, service requirements, and commercial objectives
  • Coordinating strategy check‑ins with subject matter experts to provide external perspectives, market insight, and forward‑looking recommendations
  • Reviewing stewardship reports, performance data, and service metrics to find opportunities for improvement and additional value creation
  • Orchestrating internal teams across domiciles, Global Capability Centres, and wider Aon businesses to deliver integrated client outcomes
  • Finding opportunities to strengthen client relationships, improve account profitability, and expand relevant Aon services
  • Translating technical, financial, and performance information into clear client narratives and actionable recommendations
  • Coaching and supporting more junior colleagues to strengthen client leadership capability and consistency of service delivery
  • Maintaining delivery discipline across service schedules, governance commitments, and regulatory requirements

How this opportunity is different

This role is differentiated by the level of client influence, strategic ownership, and cross‑functional coordination involved. You will operate as the central connector between captive clients and Aon, bringing together expertise from across the organization to support better client decisions and stronger long‑term partnerships.

The role is shifting from transactional service delivery toward consultative client leadership. Success depends on your ability to deeply understand client priorities, proactively find opportunities, and build value through strategic conversations, insight‑led communication, and effective orchestration of Aon capabilities.

You will help shape the future‑state client leadership model within ACIM, supporting a more proactive, data-driven, and commercially focused approach to client engagement.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Demonstrated advisory client engagement, building deep understanding of client priorities, challenges, and risk financing objectives and operating as a trusted advisor
  • Strong strategic and commercial thinking, connecting client strategies, commercial opportunities, and Aon capabilities to create measurable value and support profitable growth
  • Confirmed ability to orchestrate expertise across a matrixed organization, influencing without formal authority and aligning teams around shared client objectives

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $70,000 to $85,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Norwell, MA
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, paid holidays

Full job description

Job Description

Posting Description

Who We Are:

NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. To learn more, please visit: https://www.NFP.com.

Summary of Role:

Advance your career as an Account Manager at NFP, where you will do more than work with others — you will encourage excellent client experiences. Immerse yourself in a role that blends technology with personalized service, ensuring each client feels uniquely valued. As a pivotal member of our account management team, your role is to nurture client relationships. You will ensure their happiness and build their dedication to our brand. In this role, you will handle your own portfolio of clients, taking charge of the day-to-day interactions and becoming their go-to for exceptional service. Your responsibility extends beyond mere management; you will be the cornerstone of our promise to deliver outstanding service, working seamlessly across various operational teams. Be the difference, be the change, be part of our dynamic team!

*This is a fully remote role, with the ability to work EST working hours.*

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Work with senior team members to prepare and send the request for proposals to applicable insurance carriers and spreadsheets results as they come in.
  • Learns to review contracts, benefit plan summaries, and carrier source documents for accuracy under the direction of the Account Executive or Advisor. At this level, they will begin to learn more complex compliance and regulatory policy language.
  • Creates and maintain client files in accordance with office procedures. May be responsible for keeping client policy records
  • Takes the lead on answering questions from clients and/or insurance company personnel such as ID card request, claims or billing questions
  • Begins to develop ongoing relationships with clients. Coordinates with Senior Account Manager, Account Executives or Advisors in doing so.
  • Begins to develop relationships with carrier representatives to better understand available products and services in the marketplace and recommend them to clients
  • Learns vendor/carrier products and services from the more senior Account Manager or Account Executive.
  • Begins to review and analyze requests for proposals and insurance plan analyses. Participates in negotiations with carriers and recommend renewal actions, under the direction of a senior team member.
  • May assist Account Manager in drafting renewal presentations
  • Assist with creating and updating benefits related guides, education resources for clients
  • Learns how to conduct annual client compliance audits using NFP portal, assists more senior Account Managers in preparing document
  • Attend to client requests including product or vendor service or performance challenges
  • File form 5500 filing, reaching out for assistance as needed.
  • Participates in client projects such as implementation of new business, open enrollment process, non-discrimination testing, etc. under the direction of more senior team members
  • Create monthly, quarterly and annual reports for client review as needed
  • Distribute monthly / quarterly newsletters and other briefings and content as appropriate
  • Assist with creation of client corporate wellness programs and offerings

Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities:

  • Knowledge of benefits administration, HealthCare Reform, industry trends, carrier products and services
  • Ability to work independently and anticipate client and team needs
  • Effective time management and decision making skills
  • Diligent follow-up skills
  • Ability to express ideas clearly in both written and oral communications
  • Strong Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills
  • Commanding presentation and public speaking abilities

Education and/or Experience:

  • Associates degree (or equivalent), and BA/BS preferred
  • More than 3 years' client service and/or industry and product line experience

Certificates, Licenses, Registration:

  • Appropriately licensed or ability to obtain licensing if required

What We Offer:

We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $70,000 to $85,000. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives.

Job Description

Posting Description

Who We Are:

NFP, an Aon company, is a multiple Best Places to Work award winner in Business Insurance who has also earned the WORK180 employer endorsement. We are an organization of consultative advisors and problem solvers. We help companies and individuals around the globe address their most significant risk, workforce, wealth management and retirement challenges through custom solutions and a people-first approach. Summary of Role:

Ready to jump into the heart of our vibrant account servicing team as a Senior Account Manager? Here's your chance to become a superstar in a workplace that's all about growth, collaboration, and, of course, a little fun along the way! Join our dynamic team as a Senior Account Manager and become a vital part of our collaborative culture that thrives on fostering professional growth opportunities for our employees.

As a Senior Account Manager, you'll play a pivotal role in working closely with our Advisors and Account Executives to provide exceptional service to our valued clients. In this exciting role, you will take charge of the renewal and marketing process from inception to completion, working in tandem with our Account Executives and Advisors. Additionally, you'll have the exciting opportunity to craft materials for presentations and communications, supporting your fellow team members in day-to-day client servicing.

But that's not all – as a Senior Account Manager, you'll step into a leadership role, leading open enrollment presentations and overseeing the OE communication process. Your active participation in client meetings will be instrumental in building and maintaining strong relationships with our clients and carrier contacts. Moreover, you'll proactively drive efficient and effective service delivery to our clients.

*This is a fully remote role, with the ability to work EST working hours.*

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Works proactively to maintain relationships with carrier and client contacts. Takes significant role in meetings and on calls. Communicates directly with clients and vendors.
  • The Senior Account Manager will have responsibility for managing the renewal and marketing process from start to finish, in conjunction with the Account Executives and Advisors.
  • Reviews, benefit plan summaries, and carrier source documents for accuracy. Understands more difficult and complex regulatory language and rules.
  • May have an assigned book of business.
  • May serve as a mentor to more junior team members, trains more junior team members.
  • Develops and maintains ongoing relationships with clients and their employees. Communicates directly with them and relies on a growing knowledge of the details of various insurance coverages.
  • Develops relationships with carrier representatives in order to better understand available products and services in the marketplace and recommend them to clients
  • Acts as the subject matter expert on benefits and vendor/carrier products and services. Gets assistance on complex situations or products from more senior team members
  • Begin to anticipate client needs, works with Account Executives / Advisors to resolve.
  • Reviews request for proposals and insurance plan analyses, negotiate with carriers and recommend renewal actions.
  • Drafts client presentations in collaboration with Account Executives or Advisors; takes active role in client meetings
  • Update benefit guides, ensure client resources and communications are up to date following open enrollment or coverage change
  • Prepare document and data for annual client compliance audits to be presented by Account Executive, may take active role in presentation
  • Attend to client requests including product or vendor service or performance challenges
  • Ensure 5500 form is filed and completed in a timely manner
  • May provide updates to clients regarding appropriate industry trends and events, including all state and federal regulatory issues
  • Understands and articulates alternative funding strategies.
  • Proactive client service support in conjunction with the account management team
  • Oversees client projects such as implementation of new business, open enrollment process, non-discrimination testing, etc.
  • Interprets plan rules to ensure compliance with Plan Documents and Summary Plan Descriptions
  • Provides informal leadership and training to more junior team members, based on experience, without official supervisory responsibility.

Knowledge, Skills, and/or Abilities:

  • Knowledge of benefits administration, HealthCare Reform, industry trends, carrier products and services
  • Ability to work independently and anticipate client and team needs
  • Effective time management and decision making skills
  • Diligent follow up skills
  • Ability to express ideas clearly in both written and oral communications
  • Strong Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills
  • Commanding presentation and public speaking abilities

Education and/or Experience:

  • BA/BS preferred
  • Typically more than five years industry and product line experience

Certificates, Licenses, Registration:

  • Life, Accident and Health Insurance License required.

What We Offer:

We're proud to offer a competitive salary, PTO & paid holidays, 401(k) with match, exclusive discount programs, health & wellness programs, and more. Our PeopleFirst culture focuses on building and nurturing lifelong relationships with our employees because, at the end of the day, we exist to be there for others. The base salary range for this position is $80,000 – $98,500. The base salary offered will be determined by factors including, but not limited to, experience, credentials, education, certifications, skill level required for the position, the scope of the position, and geographic location. Actual base salary offered will be determined on a case-by-case basis. In addition to the base salary, this position may be eligible for performance-based incentives.
